newsitem.title: TURKEY: Iraqi tanks surround captured northern town - PUK.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi tanks surround captured northern town - PUK.

text.p: Iraqi tanks were digging in around the Kurdish town of Koi Sanjaq after Baghdad-backed Kurds seized it in heavy fighting at the weekend, the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) faction said on Monday.

"Eyewitnesss reports from the town of Koi Sanjaq, which was occupied...by Saddam-Barzani forces, state that Iraqi tanks and armoured vehicles are currently surrounding the town. The eyewitnesses have counted more than 50 tanks and armoured vehicles," the PUK said in a statement faxed from London.

Forces of Massoud Barzani's Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) -- who were aided by President Saddam Hussein's troops in an attack on August 31 to take the main northern city of Arbil -- captured the towns of Koi Sanjaq and Degala from the rival PUK on Sunday.
Thousands of Kurds fled from the embattled towns in cars, trucks and even bulldozers.
"We call on the U.S.-led coalition to move urgently, before its too late, to stop the Iraqi onslaught. Urgent and decisive help is needed," the PUK said.
The United States warned Baghdad it would not hesitate to strike against any Iraqi aggression but said it could not confirm reports of an Iraqi role in the fresh Kurdish fighting.
The KDP has denied Iraqi involvment in the weekend fighting.
Koi Sanjaq, a city of 80,000, fell hours after the KDP seized the village of Degala.
Koi Sanjaq is 100 km (65 miles) northwest of Sulaimaniya, the PUK's last remaining stronghold in the Iraqi north.
American forces last week fired 44 cruise missiles at southern Iraq to retaliate for what Washington said was Saddam's role in helping the KDP seize Arbil from the PUK.
